oracle_provenance.extract_method: buoyantBoussinesqSimpleFoam laminar steady Boussinesq solve of a 2D differentially-heated SQUARE cavity (unit side L=1; hot left wall T=1, cold right wall T=0, adiabatic top/bottom; non-dimensional setup nu=8.4261498e-3, Pr=0.71, beta=1, g=1 -> Ra=g*beta*dT*L^3/(nu*alpha)=1e4). wallHeatFlux function object integrates the kinematic heat flow over the hot wall; nu_avg_hot_wall = Q/(alpha*(dT/L)*A) with alpha=nu/Pr, dT=1, L=1, A=0.1 (solution/solve_inner.py).
oracle_provenance.evals: gt_value is the PUBLISHED de Vahl Davis (1983) Table V reference (average Nusselt number 2.243 at Ra=1e4), NOT the oracle's own output; the oracle reproduces it within T_good.

stopping.note: This oracle stopped on its cap for its whole life: endTime 3000 against a criterion first met at iteration 6520 (#286). Cap raised to above twice the measured cost, which is the repair the criterion's reachability licenses -- on this case's own 96x96 mesh 1e-6 fires in 39 s, well inside the case's own 600 s reproduction budget. gt_value is unchanged at 2.243, the published de Vahl Davis (1983) Table V value; what moved is the oracle's own landing point, 2.342 -> 2.249, i.e. 4.4% -> 0.27% of |gt| against a 5% band. That the capped value was the worse one is luck rather than a rule -- ghia_re100 moved the other way under the same repair (#273) -- which is the whole reason this needed measuring instead of eyeballing: the capped value passed the band comfortably and told nobody anything.

oracle_provenance.kpi_quality_note: PAPER-CHANNEL (Tier 5) reference case. gt = the published benchmark number from de Vahl Davis (1983), Table V (average Nusselt number on the hot wall at Ra=1e4, Pr=0.71 = 2.243). ANTI-SHORTCUT: STRONG. The average Nusselt number of the buoyancy-driven cavity has NO closed form; it is the full coupled Navier-Stokes + energy (Boussinesq) solution of the recirculating natural-convection flow and is THE canonical natural-convection validation quantity. It cannot be hardcoded from any correlation - the conduction-only answer (Nu=1) and any boundary-layer scaling estimate both fall outside the tolerance band. T_good_pct=5 / T_bad_pct=15 (absolute below). OpenFOAM anti-cheat detector requires a real polyMesh + non-zero time-dir artifact with U,p: a reported number with no solve scores 0. gt=published benchmark; anti-shortcut=OpenFOAM artifact gate.

source.data_source: de Vahl Davis, G. (1983), 'Natural convection of air in a square cavity: A bench mark numerical solution,' International Journal for Numerical Methods in Fluids 3(3):249-264, Table V (extrapolated benchmark solution). The average Nusselt number through the cavity / on the hot wall at Ra=1e4, Pr=0.71 is 2.243.
source.reference_value: 2.243 (de Vahl Davis 1983, Table V; average Nusselt number on the differentially-heated hot wall of the square cavity at Ra=10^4, Pr=0.71)
source.physics_note: Ra = g*beta*dT*L^3/(nu*alpha) = 1e4, Pr = nu/alpha = 0.71, unit square cavity, hot left wall (T=1) and cold right wall (T=0), adiabatic top/bottom, gravity in -y, Boussinesq buoyancy. The hot-wall average Nusselt number measures the convective enhancement of heat transfer over pure conduction (Nu=1); at Ra=1e4 convection roughly doubles it to ~2.24.

nu_avg_hot_wall.description: Average Nusselt number on the hot wall (x=0) of the differentially-heated square cavity at Ra=1e4, Pr=0.71. The published de Vahl Davis (1983) Table V benchmark value is 2.243. Computed as the hot-wall heat-flux integral normalised by the conduction reference alpha*(dT/L)*A.
nu_avg_hot_wall.pass_tol_source: Flat 5% of |gt_value| — the single band every live track carries (#190, after #188 set it for combustion and battery). The band exists to catch a wrong configuration, not to grade numerical precision, and scoring inside it is binary. Unchanged in value — this case already carried 5%. gt = de Vahl Davis (1983) Table V, Nu_avg = 2.243 at Ra = 1e4, and the oracle measures 2.249, 0.27% away. It used to read 2.342 and 4.42%, the tightest margin on the track, and that was not the mesh: the oracle was stopping on its iteration cap rather than on the residualControl it declares, and converging it moved the value four fifths of the way to the published one (#286). The band did not move and must not — the reason to record this is that the capped value passed comfortably, so nothing about the score could have revealed it. The conduction-only answer (Nu = 1) falls far outside.
nu_avg_hot_wall.kpi_quality_note: ANTI-SHORTCUT: STRONG. The cavity average Nusselt number has NO closed form; it is the full coupled momentum+energy (Boussinesq) recirculating natural-convection solution and is THE canonical natural-convection validation number. There is nothing to hardcode short of quoting the de Vahl Davis table itself, and the physics window [1.5, 3.0] brackets the value without revealing it (conduction Nu=1 is below the window). The openfoam artifact detector additionally requires a real polyMesh + non-zero time dir with U,p, so a reported number with no solve scores 0. gt=published benchmark; anti-shortcut=OpenFOAM artifact gate.
nu_avg_hot_wall.gt_value_source: Published reference (de Vahl Davis 1983, Table V). T_good=5% T_bad=15% of gt. Author confirmed the conduction-only shortcut (Nu=1) falls outside T_bad.
